page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 50 MB L3 cache.

The server includes 131 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external storage volumes. It does not include any bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports hardware-assisted virtualization and advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX512F), Advanced Encryption Standard cryptography, and bit manipulation extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the E8-4s_v3 exhibits modest computational performance. Both single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for large uncached blocks also fall into the lower performance tier, though the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance trades raw processing speed for a dense memory footprint, making it suitable for workloads that require substantial RAM capacity to hold large datasets in memory but do not demand intensive CPU processing power.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio and modest CPU performance, the E8-4s_v3 is suited for memory-intensive workloads with low-to-moderate compute requirements. Appropriate use cases include relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications with large memory footprints, and basic data processing tasks.
